nodes.title: Online/offline detection docs do not mention `net.isOnline`
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/21004 added a `net.isOnline` method to the main process in 2020.

The electron docs for [Online/Offline Event Detection](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/tutorial/online-offline-events) only discuss the renderer process `navigator.onLine` attribute and further note:

https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/9b740594fbdd0a205a1c2062c27184bb691a0b05/docs/tutorial/online-offline-events.md?plain=1#L87


### Proposed Solution

The Online/Offline Event Detection should note both the main and renderer methods for detecting whether the system is online. Further, they should include whether the methods will produce different results and whether one is more reliable than the other.

### Alternatives Considered

NA

### Additional Information

_No response_

nodes.title: Custom cursors revert to default when intersecting the top screen edge in kiosk mode
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

38.2.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS Tahoe 26.0.1

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

When using a custom cursor in the kiosk mode of a webpage, I expect to have an immersive experience, and the custom cursor should ensure normal display regardless of which edge of the screen it touches.

### Actual Behavior

This is the problem I encountered while developing a macOS game based on Electron. When using a custom cursor in the kiosk mode of a webpage, if the cursor's outline intersects with the top edge of the screen, it unexpectedly reverts to the default system cursor. This issue significantly affects the gaming experience. In my game, I need a full-screen immersive gaming experience, where the custom cursor is crucial for maintaining immersion and the game's artistic style. However, this limitation causes the cursor to change abruptly when it touches the top boundary. This problem is particularly evident in large custom cursors, as macOS's default cursor is relatively small, making the switch more sudden and disrupting the player's immersion. I sincerely hope this issue can be resolved, as there will be many Electron games.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a3d56d52-7a80-4e59-b7cb-536b9ccc031a)

nodes.title: Support type="module" for <webview> to allow native ES Modules
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Currently, the `<webview>` tag in Electron does not support native ES Modules. This forces developers using pure ESM projects to:
* Create additional preload scripts to import modules,
* Use `require()` (CommonJS), or
* Use `webview.executeJavaScript('import(...)')`, which is less clean and error-prone.
This creates inconsistencies in modern projects that adopt ESM in **renderer**, **main**, and **webview**, making migration and maintenance more difficult.

### Proposed Solution

Add support for a `type="module"` attribute on `<webview>`, similar to `<script type="module">`. Example usage:
```html
<webview
  src="https://example.com/app.js"
  type="module"
  nodeintegration="false"
  preload="./preload.mjs"
></webview>
```

Benefits:
1. Allows importing ES Modules directly inside the `<webview>` without workarounds.
2. Simplifies integration with modern frameworks (React, Vue, Svelte) using ESM.
3. Improves consistency between `BrowserWindow` and `<webview>`.
4. Reduces complexity of preload scripts and module management.

Technical consideration:
* Should be optional to avoid breaking CommonJS projects.
* Must respect existing sandbox and contextIsolation restrictions.
* Ideally compatible with both static and dynamic `import()` statements.

### Alternatives Considered

* Using preload scripts as modules (`.mjs`) and manually importing everything.
* Executing `import()` dynamically via `webview.executeJavaScript()`.
* Mixing CommonJS (`require()`) with ESM using Node’s `createRequire`.

All of these are workarounds and introduce complexity or potential errors, especially in fully ESM-based projects.

### Additional Information

This feature would make `<webview>` more aligned with the modern JavaScript ecosystem and significantly improve developer experience for Electron apps built entirely with ES Modules.

Windows ### Operating System Version Windows 11 ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version N/A ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? I don't know how to test ### Expected Behavior `systemPreferences.getAccentColor` should return the accent color as it is set in the Windows settings. I saw some possibly somewhat related issues, but those usually mentioned slightly off colors, not completely different hues. ### Actual Behavior `systemPreferences.getAccentColor` returns very often wrong colors. Cyan turns into yellow, yellow turns into green, green turns into yellow. The only color I have tested that works is purple. It almost seems as if Electron retrieves values with a hue-shift. I'm usually not working on Windows, so I didn't notice that until a user informed me today that this happens. See below for a few screenshots. ### Testcase Gist URL _No response_ ### Additional Information Here are just two examples. On the left side you can see the personalization settings on my Win11 machine. On the right side, you can see how the accent color looks like rendered. On the bottom you can see the raw value as it is returned from the API.

### Electron Version

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Reproduction steps

1. Start local http / websocket servers with following config:
```
const http = require('http');
const { WebSocketServer } = require('ws');

const server = http.createServer();

const wss = new WebSocketServer({ noServer: true });

server.on('upgrade', (req, socket, head) => {
  const auth = req.headers['authorization'] || '';
  const expected = 'Basic ' + Buffer.from('user:pass').toString('base64');

  if (auth !== expected) {
    // Respond with proper 401 for WebSocket handshake
    socket.write(
      'HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized\r\n' +
      'WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="Test"\r\n' +
      'Content-Length: 0\r\n' +
      '\r\n'
    );
    socket.destroy();
    return;
  }

  // Accept the WebSocket upgrade
  wss.handleUpgrade(req, socket, head, (ws) => {
    wss.emit('connection', ws, req);
  });
});

wss.on('connection', ws => {
  ws.send('Authenticated!');
});

server.listen(8080, () => console.log('Auth WebSocket server running on ws://localhost:8080'));
```

[web_socket.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22798719/web_socket.zip)

nodes.title: Add support for macOS 26 .icon format in app.dock.setIcon()
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

macOS 26 introduced the new layered .icon format (supports tinted variants). Electron’s nativeImage / app.dock.setIcon() can’t load .icon, forcing developers to ship pre-rendered images and lose system-driven variants.

### Proposed Solution

Add .icon support to nativeImage and allow app.dock.setIcon() to accept a .icon path or nativeImage created from .icon. Preserve variant selection automatically.

### Alternatives Considered

Pre-render variant PNGs and switch at runtime with dock.setIcon() loses dynamic system rendering and increases asset maintenance.

### Additional Information

electron-builder will support new format https://github.com/electron-userland/electron-builder/pull/9279

nodes.title: Utilize the macOS Keychain for ASAR Integrity
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

While ASAR Integrity is a great feature, on macOS is uses the `Info.plist` file to store the expected hash. This works, I see two potential issues with it:
1. While, theoretically, `.app` packages are sealed on macOS, depending on certain configurations, the `Info.plist` can be editable by an outside app. Secondarily, it seems macOS does not check the integrity of `.app` package files on every launch, so an attacker could just find a way to modify the `app.asar` *and* the `Info.plist` and negate the ASAR Integrity check.
2. This could limit some custom auto-update solutions. While many auto-update solutions I have seen on Electron do work at the package level (meaning a new `.app` for each version), I have seen some that seem to mostly switch out JS files behind the scenes.

### Proposed Solution

I believe a better candidate for storage of the hash (at least on macOS) is the Keychain. By default, keychain items made by an app are only accessible by that app (unless the user explicitly changes an ACL). This would thwart most bad actors' attempts at changing the hash after compromising the `.asar` archive. While not totally foolproof (an attacker could socially engineer the user into giving up access to the keychain item containing the hash), I believe its better than the `Info.plist` method. Additionally, the macOS Keychain is already uses as part of [the safeStorage API](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/safe-storage), so I don't believe using it for ASAR integrity would be that difficult. Utilizing the keychain would also help those who don't switch out their `Info.plist` each time they update their `.asar` archive (theoretical, at this point).

### Alternatives Considered

N/A

### Additional Information

I'm a security researcher, first and foremost. While I do have fairly good software engineering experience, there may be certain blockers or quirks of Electron that make my proposed solution difficult to implement. I am open and willing to collaboratively discuss and adjust this feature request as needed.

nodes.body:

- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

30

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

Mac

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

28.3.3

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

I’ve identified a performance issue that only occurs in the macOS distribution build when using Electron 30.x or newer.

During development, the application runs smoothly — there are no signs of slowness or visible errors.
However, once the compiled version (.app or .pkg) is generated and executed on macOS, it becomes extremely slow, with long delays when loading screens or interacting with the interface, as if it were running with very limited system resources.

This behavior only affects macOS; the same build performs normally on Windows and Linux.
So far, I haven’t been able to determine the exact cause. There are no errors in the console and nothing that clearly points to a dependency or compatibility issue.

At this stage, the main difficulty is that I can’t find a clear way to debug this issue.
The application doesn’t show any errors in the console, either during the build process or at runtime in macOS.

I’ve tried checking both:

The build logs generated by electron-builder.

The macOS Console app for system-level logs when launching the compiled .app.

So far, nothing indicates what could be causing the slowdown — everything seems to work correctly except for the very poor performance of the distributed build.

I’m not sure if there’s a specific way to enable more detailed logs for Electron in production mode or if I should try to run the packaged app with extra flags or profiling tools to get more information.

### Actual Behavior

I don’t know why the installers or executables are so slow.

nodes.body:

### Electron Version

38.2.1

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 26

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

33.0.0-nightly.20240814 (broken in 33.0.0-nightly.20240815)

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

When using `shell.openExternal()` with an app schema of an app _not installed_, I would expect an exception to the raised _without_ triggering the [system modal](https://share.cleanshot.com/6rvdX5TZ) "There is no application set to open the URL..." 

### Actual Behavior

A [system modal](https://share.cleanshot.com/6rvdX5TZ) is triggered every time, and it does not look like there is a way to avoid it. This prevents us from implementing an automatic fallback to the browser, where our app would first try to open a third-party app (e.g. Todoist) and fall back on the browser if this failed. 
This was working smoothly up to Electron 32. From Electron 33, it looks like this system message is triggered every time, which is annoying for our users.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/74cfcb6acbee70cb409714eee22f5acc

### Additional Information

I managed to track down the change in behavior between 33.0.0-nightly.20240814 (no macOS system dialog triggered) and 33.0.0-nightly.20240815 (macOS system dialog triggered).
